Dr.B Townsed

The Emergency Department

Newtown Children Hospital



10/04/2010



Dear Dr. Townsed,



Re:Emma Johnson



            I am writing to urgently refer Emma, an 11-year-old girl, whose symptoms and signs are
consistent with sever asthma. Your expert assessment would be valued.



Today, Emma presented at my clinic with worsening shortness of breath and obvious use of the
accessory muscles. She has had wheezing over the previous two days and fever ,along with runny nose.
Additionally, loss of appetite was reported. Her chest auscultation revealed a widspread wheeze with no
focal signs ,and the PEFR has markedly diminished to 140 l/min. Nebulized Ventolin has showed
minimal improvement in her condition.



Initially, on30/11/2009, Emma presented complaining of a nocturnal cough ,which had worsened over
the following weeeks. Consequently, diagnosis of asthma was suggested. I commenced her on Ventolin
,which slightly improved her symptoms. Her PEFR increased from 230 to 280 l/min. Inhaled
corticosteroid was added as her asthma was still unstable.



Two months earlier, Emma's condition was stable. Her asthma was well- controlled on Becotide200 two
puffs three times per day and Ventolin ,when needed. Her PEFR was 340l/min.



Emma has no known allergies ,and her mother as well asold sister are asthmatic.



I would be grateful if you could manage Emma’s condition. Should there be any queries, kindly do not
hesitate to contact me .
 Yours sincerely,

Doctor
